claim: Nicotinic partial agonists provide an accepted aid for smoking cessation and contribute to decreasing tobacco-related disease.
source_text: Nicotinic partial agonists provide an accepted aid for smoking cessation and thus contribute to decreasing tobacco-related disease.
evidence_reasoning: This statement reflects established medical knowledge about the clinical use of nicotinic partial agonists for smoking cessation.

claim: There was no reductionist method to examine the cellular and subcellular pharmacokinetic properties of nicotinic partial agonists in living cells prior to this work.
source_text: However, there remains no reductionist method to examine the cellular and subcellular pharmacokinetic properties of these compounds in living cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about the state of the field prior to the current study, representing a gap in existing methodology.

claim: The authors developed new intensity-based drug-sensing fluorescent reporters (iDrugSnFRs) for dianicline, cytisine, 10-fluorocytisine, and 9-bromo-10-ethylcytisine.
source_text: Here, we developed new intensity-based drug-sensing fluorescent reporters (iDrugSnFRs) for the nicotinic partial agonists dianicline, cytisine, and two cytisine derivatives – 10-fluorocytisine and 9-bromo-10-ethylcytisine.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: This study reports the first atomic-scale structures of liganded periplasmic binding protein-based biosensors.
source_text: We report the first atomic-scale structures of liganded periplasmic binding protein-based biosensors, accelerating development of iDrugSnFRs and also explaining the activation mechanism.
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding supported by crystallographic data presented in the manuscript (PDB entries 7S7U, 7S7T).

claim: The nicotinic iDrugSnFRs detect their drug partners in solution, at the plasma membrane, and in the endoplasmic reticulum of cell lines and mouse hippocampal neurons.
source_text: The nicotinic iDrugSnFRs detect their drug partners in solution, as well as at the plasma membrane (PM) and in the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) of cell lines and mouse hippocampal neurons.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data from fluorescence imaging experiments in HeLa cells, HEK293T cells, and primary hippocampal neurons.

claim: At the plasma membrane, the speed of solution changes limits the growth and decay rates of the fluorescence response in almost all cases.
source_text: At the PM, the speed of solution changes limits the growth and decay rates of the fluorescence response in almost all cases.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from time-resolved fluorescence measurements showing rapid kinetics at the PM.

claim: Rates of membrane crossing differ among nicotinic drugs by more than 30-fold.
source_text: In contrast, we found that rates of membrane crossing differ among these nicotinic drugs by >30-fold.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding based on comparative kinetic measurements of different drugs crossing cellular membranes.

claim: Partial agonists with lower efficacy than nicotine could serve as effective smoking-cessation drugs.
source_text: Prior work suggests that partial agonists with lower efficacy than nicotine could serve as effective smoking-cessation drugs (Rose et al., 1994), and efforts continue in that direction (Rollema and Hurst, 2018).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to prior published work by Rose et al., 1994 and Rollema and Hurst, 2018.

claim: Cytisine is an α4β2 nAChR partial agonist.
source_text: Another plant alkaloid, (-)-cytisine (also called cytisinicline and Tabex), an α4β2 nAChR partial agonist, served as a basis for the synthesis of analogs that have not yet entered the clinic
evidence_reasoning: This is established pharmacological knowledge about cytisine's mechanism of action.

claim: Varenicline is currently the only FDA-approved smoking-cessation drug.
source_text: Varenicline (Chantix) has four rings, two more than nicotine or cytisine, and is currently the only FDA-approved smoking-cessation drug, but the modest quit rate of ~18% at 12 months invites further investigation
evidence_reasoning: This is a statement about regulatory approval status and clinical efficacy, supported by citation to Coe et al., 2005 and Mills et al., 2009.

claim: Varenicline has a quit rate of approximately 18% at 12 months.
source_text: Varenicline (Chantix) has four rings, two more than nicotine or cytisine, and is currently the only FDA-approved smoking-cessation drug, but the modest quit rate of ~18% at 12 months invites further investigation
evidence_reasoning: This is a clinical outcome statistic referenced from prior studies (Coe et al., 2005; Mills et al., 2009).

claim: Dianicline was discontinued after unfavorable Phase III clinical trials.
source_text: Dianicline, another tetracyclic compound, was discontinued after unfavorable Phase III clinical trials (Cohen et al., 2003; Fagerstrom and Balfour, 2006).
evidence_reasoning: This is a historical fact about drug development supported by citations to Cohen et al., 2003 and Fagerstrom and Balfour, 2006.

claim: A nicotinic ligand for smoking cessation must enter the brain where the most nicotine-sensitive nAChRs (α4β2) occur.
source_text: A nicotinic ligand for smoking cessation must satisfy at least three criteria (Rollema et al., 2010; Tashkin, 2015). (1) It must enter the brain, where the most nicotine-sensitive nAChRs (α4β2) occur.
evidence_reasoning: This criterion is cited from Rollema et al., 2010 and Tashkin, 2015, and reflects established pharmacological requirements.

claim: A nicotinic ligand for smoking cessation must activate α4β2 nAChRs with an EC50 sufficient to reduce cravings and withdrawal (1–2 μM).
source_text: It must also (2) activate α4β2 nAChRs with an EC50 sufficient to reduce cravings and withdrawal (1–2 μM).
evidence_reasoning: This criterion is cited from Rollema et al., 2010 and Tashkin, 2015.

claim: A nicotinic ligand for smoking cessation must block nicotine binding to reduce the reward phase of smoking (2–30 min).
source_text: Finally, it must (3) block nicotine binding to reduce the reward phase of smoking (2–30 min).
evidence_reasoning: This criterion is cited from Rollema et al., 2010 and Tashkin, 2015.

claim: Varenicline meets all three criteria for smoking-cessation drugs.
source_text: Varenicline meets these criteria, while cytisine (low brain penetration) and dianicline (EC50 = 18 μM) each fail one of the criteria (Rollema et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative assessment cited from Rollema et al., 2010.

claim: Cytisine fails the brain penetration criterion for smoking-cessation drugs.
source_text: Varenicline meets these criteria, while cytisine (low brain penetration) and dianicline (EC50 = 18 μM) each fail one of the criteria (Rollema et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific limitation of cytisine cited from Rollema et al., 2010.

claim: Dianicline has an EC50 of 18 μM and fails the EC50 criterion for smoking-cessation drugs.
source_text: Varenicline meets these criteria, while cytisine (low brain penetration) and dianicline (EC50 = 18 μM) each fail one of the criteria (Rollema et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a specific pharmacological property and limitation of dianicline cited from Rollema et al., 2010.

claim: For uncharged molecules, the conventional metric for membrane permeability is logP, where P is the octanol-water partition coefficient.
source_text: For uncharged molecules, the conventional metric for membrane permeability is logP, where P is the octanol-water partition coefficient.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in pharmacology and medicinal chemistry.

claim: For weak bases including most orally available neural drugs, logP must be corrected to account for the fraction of uncharged molecules at pH 7.4, resulting in the metric logDpH7.4.
source_text: For weak bases including most orally available neural drugs, logP must be corrected to account for the fraction of uncharged (deprotonated) molecules at the pH of interest, usually pH 7.4; the resulting metric, termed logDpH7.4, is always less positive than logP.
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge in pharmaceutical chemistry about how to calculate membrane permeability for ionizable compounds.

claim: 10-fluorocytisine and 9-bromo-10-ethylcytisine have cytisine-like EC50 for α4β2 nAChRs but more positive calculated logDpH7.4 values, suggesting greater membrane permeability.
source_text: Two of the resulting derivatives, 10-fluorocytisine and 9-bromo-10-ethylcytisine, have cytisine-like EC50 for the α4β2 nAChRs, but more positive calculated logDpH7.4 values, suggesting greater membrane permeability at the nearly neutral pH of the blood, brain, and cytoplasm (Blom et al., 2019).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from prior work by Blom et al., 2019, combining experimental EC50 data with calculated logD values.

claim: Estimates of logDpH7.4 are inexact, extrapolated, or rely on algorithmic calculations whose results differ over 2 log units for individual molecules.
source_text: Estimates of logDpH7.4 are inexact, extrapolated, or rely on algorithmic calculations whose results differ over 2 log units for individual molecules (Pieńko et al., 2016).
evidence_reasoning: This is a limitation of computational methods cited from Pieńko et al., 2016.

claim: Nicotine enters the endoplasmic reticulum, binds to nascent nAChRs, becomes a pharmacological chaperone, and eventually causes selective upregulation of these receptors on the plasma membrane.
source_text: Nicotine itself (logDpH7.4 0.99) enters the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), binds to nascent nAChRs, becomes a pharmacological chaperone for the nAChRs, and eventually causes selective upregulation of these receptors on the plasma membrane (PM) (Henderson and Lester, 2015).
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic description of nicotine's effects cited from Henderson and Lester, 2015.

claim: Nicotine has a logDpH7.4 of 0.99.
source_text: Nicotine itself (logDpH7.4 0.99) enters the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)
evidence_reasoning: This is a calculated physicochemical property of nicotine.

claim: Nicotine and varenicline enter the ER within seconds of drug application and exit equally rapidly from the ER upon extracellular washing.
source_text: We previously explored the subcellular pharmacokinetics of nicotine and varenicline in immortalized cell lines and cultured neurons using the iDrugSnFRs iNicSnFR3a and iNicSnFR3b to visualize that these nicotinic agonists enter the ER within seconds of drug application and exit equally rapidly from the ER upon extracellular washing (Shivange et al., 2019).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from the authors' prior work cited as Shivange et al., 2019.

claim: Nicotine crosses six plasma membranes to enter the brain within 20 seconds.
source_text: That nicotine diffuses across cellular membranes in seconds has been suspected for decades: nicotine crosses six PMs to enter the brain within 20 s, providing a 'buzz.'
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about nicotine pharmacokinetics, though the manuscript notes it has been 'suspected for decades' rather than definitively proven.

claim: Varenicline becomes trapped in acidic vesicles.
source_text: That varenicline becomes trapped in acidic vesicles suggests appreciable membrane permeation but may also underlie unwanted effects (Govind et al., 2017; Le Houezec, 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding cited from Govind et al., 2017 and Le Houezec, 2003.

claim: Crystals of iNicSnFR3adt in the presence of 10 mM nicotine diffracted to 2.95 Å resolution.
source_text: Crystals of iNicSnFR3adt in the presence of 10 mM nicotine diffracted to 2.95 Å resolution (PDB 7S7U).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct experimental result from X-ray crystallography.

claim: The liganded periplasmic binding protein domain of iNicSnFR3adt adopts a closed conformation.
source_text: Overall, the liganded periplasmic binding protein (PBP) domain of iNicSnFR3adt adopts a closed conformation (Figure 1A).
evidence_reasoning: This is a structural observation from crystallographic data.

claim: An 'avocado'-shaped electron density was observed in the nicotine binding site, enclosed by several aromatic residues.
source_text: In the binding pocket between the top and bottom lobes of the PBP, we observed an 'avocado'-shaped electron density in the nicotine binding site, enclosed by several aromatic residues (Figure 1B).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from electron density maps in the crystal structure.

claim: The combination of protonation/deprotonation and the rotatable bond of nicotine vitiate unambiguously localizing it within the binding pocket.
source_text: The combination of protonation/deprotonation and the rotatable bond of nicotine (Elmore and Dougherty, 2000) vitiate unambiguously localizing it within the binding pocket.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of the crystallographic data, with reference to known properties of nicotine from Elmore and Dougherty, 2000.

claim: Crystals of iNicSnFR3adt with varenicline bound diffracted to 3.2 Å resolution.
source_text: Crystals of iNicSnFR3adt with varenicline bound were isomorphous to those of the nicotine-bound crystals and diffracted to 3.2 Å resolution (PDB 7S7T).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct experimental result from X-ray crystallography.

claim: The rigidity and additional ring of varenicline allowed unambiguous localization in the binding pocket.
source_text: While the protein structure (Figure 1D) is identical to that of the nicotine bound structure (Figure 1A), the rigidity and additional ring of varenicline allowed us to unambiguously localize it in the binding pocket.
evidence_reasoning: This is an interpretation of crystallographic data comparing varenicline to nicotine binding.

claim: Varenicline is enclosed by the same aromatic residues as nicotine, forming cation-π interactions with Tyr65 and Tyr357.
source_text: Varenicline is enclosed by the same aromatic residues as nicotine, forming cation-π interactions with Tyr65 and Tyr357, in addition to other interactions with the pocket residues (Figure 1E).
evidence_reasoning: This is a structural observation from the crystal structure showing specific molecular interactions.

claim: Similar ligand-induced conformational changes occur in the PBP for nicotine, varenicline, ACh, and choline.
source_text: The data confirm that similar ligand-induced conformational changes occur in the PBP for nicotine, varenicline, ACh (Borden et al., 2019), and choline (Fan, 2020; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative structural analysis combining current data with cited prior work.

claim: These conformational changes resemble those for other OpuBC PBPs.
source_text: These changes resemble those for other OpuBC PBPs (Schiefner et al., 2004).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison to prior structural work on related proteins cited from Schiefner et al., 2004.

claim: In the apo state, Glu78 in Linker 1 approaches within approximately 2.5 Å of the oxygen of the tyrosine fluorophore.
source_text: In the full iDrugSnFR, in the apo state, the Glu78 in Linker 1 approaches within ~2.5 Å of the oxygen of the tyrosine fluorophore (Figure 1E1; PDB 7S7V).
evidence_reasoning: This is a structural measurement from crystallographic data of the apo state.

claim: In the liganded state, Glu78 has moved away from the fluorophore, presumably allowing the fluorescent tyrosinate to form.
source_text: Figure 1E2 provides structural details confirming the hypothesis (Barnett et al., 2017; Nasu et al., 2021) that in the liganded state Glu78 has moved away, presumably allowing the fluorescent tyrosinate to form (Video 2).
evidence_reasoning: This is a structural observation that confirms a hypothesis from prior work (Barnett et al., 2017; Nasu et al., 2021).

claim: The activation mechanism is termed the 'candle snuffer'.
source_text: We term this mechanism the 'candle snuffer'.
evidence_reasoning: This is a descriptive name given to the mechanism based on the structural observations.

claim: iDianiSnFR has an EC50 of 6.7 ± 0.3 µM, ΔFmax/F0 of 7.4 ± 0.1, and S-slope of 1.1.
source_text: The dianicline sensor, iDianiSnFR, has EC50 6.7 ± 0.3 µM, ΔFmax/F0 7.4 ± 0.1, and S-slope 1.1.
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative measurements from dose-response experiments in E. coli lysate.

claim: iCytSnFR has an EC50 of 9.4 ± 0.8 µM, ΔFmax/F0 of 5.0 ± 0.2, and S-slope of 0.5.
source_text: The cytisine sensor, iCytSnFR, has EC50 9.4 ± 0.8 µM, ΔFmax/F0 5.0 ± 0.2, and S-slope 0.5 (Table 1, Figure 2A and B).
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative measurements from dose-response experiments in E. coli lysate.

claim: iCyt_F_SnFR has an EC50 of 1.4 ± 0.04 µM, ΔFmax/F0 of 7.9 ± 0.1, and S-slope of 5.6.
source_text: This optimization gave us iCyt_F_SnFR (EC50 1.4 ± 0.04 µM, ΔFmax/F0 7.9 ± 0.1, S-slope 5.6)
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative measurements from dose-response experiments in E. coli lysate.

claim: iCyt_BrEt_SnFR has an EC50 of 5.7 ± 0.1 µM, ΔFmax/F0 of 4.0 ± 0.03, and S-slope of 0.7.
source_text: iCyt_BrEt_SnFR (EC50 5.7 ± 0.1 µM, ΔFmax/F0 4.0 ± 0.03, and S-slope 0.7)
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative measurements from dose-response experiments in E. coli lysate.

claim: iDianiSnFR showed the greatest fidelity for its drug partner among the newly developed iDrugSnFRs.
source_text: iDianiSnFR had the greatest fidelity for its drug partner but also showed an increased EC50 (15 µM) as a purified protein versus its EC50 in lysate (6.7 µM), possibly indicating decreased stability in a purified form.
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative assessment based on specificity testing against a panel of nicotinic agonists.

claim: iDianiSnFR showed an increased EC50 (15 µM) as a purified protein versus its EC50 in lysate (6.7 µM), possibly indicating decreased stability in a purified form.
source_text: iDianiSnFR had the greatest fidelity for its drug partner but also showed an increased EC50 (15 µM) as a purified protein versus its EC50 in lysate (6.7 µM), possibly indicating decreased stability in a purified form.
evidence_reasoning: The EC50 difference is experimental data, but the explanation about stability is speculative.

claim: iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR showed a greater level of promiscuity for compounds comprising the nicotinic agonist panel.
source_text: iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR showed a greater level of promiscuity for the compounds comprising the nicotinic agonist panel.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from specificity testing showing cross-reactivity with related compounds.

claim: iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR have an exceptionally low (60‒90 nM) EC50 for varenicline.
source_text: Of note, iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR have an exceptionally low (60‒90 nM) EC50 for varenicline.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement from dose-response experiments showing high affinity for varenicline.

claim: The newly developed iDrugSnFRs showed negligible binding to choline or acetylcholine.
source_text: The newly developed iDrugSnFRs showed negligible binding to choline or the neurotransmitter acetylcholine, leading one to expect minimal endogenous interference during future in vivo experiments.
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from specificity testing against endogenous molecules.

claim: iDianiSnFR showed no response to any of nine selected endogenous compounds above background.
source_text: iDianiSnFR showed no response to any of the nine selected compounds above background.
evidence_reasoning: This is a result from testing against a panel of endogenous molecules including neurotransmitters.

claim: iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR exhibited a ΔF/F0 of 0.25‒0.8 to dopamine at 316 µM/1 mM.
source_text: However, they exhibited a ΔF/F0 of 0.25‒0.8 to dopamine at 316 µM/1 mM
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement showing some cross-reactivity with dopamine at high concentrations.

claim: iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR exhibited a ΔF/F0 of 0.8–1.5 to serotonin at 316 µM/1 mM.
source_text: and a ΔF/F0 of 0.8–1.5 to serotonin (5-HT) at 316 µM/1 mM.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative measurement showing some cross-reactivity with serotonin at high concentrations.

claim: In terms of S-slope, the SnFRs are at least 250-fold more sensitive to their eponymous partners than to other molecules tested.
source_text: In terms of S-slope, the relevant metric for most cellular or in vivo experiments, the SnFRs are at least 250-fold more sensitive to their eponymous partners than to other molecules we have tested.
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison of sensitivity based on S-slope calculations from dose-response data.

claim: The experimentally determined KD of each iDrugSnFR:drug pair using ITC was within a factor of 1.5 from the experimentally determined EC50 for fluorescence.
source_text: The experimentally determined KD of each iDrugSnFR:drug pair using ITC was within a factor of 1.5 from the experimentally determined EC50 for fluorescence in E. coli lysate or purified protein (Table 3).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison of binding affinity measurements from two different experimental methods (ITC and fluorescence).

claim: The EC50 for fluorescence is dominated by the overall binding of the ligand for all the iDrugSnFRs.
source_text: We infer that the EC50 for fluorescence is dominated by the overall binding of the ligand for all the iDrugSnFRs.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the close agreement between KD and EC50 values.

claim: The heats for iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR binding were exothermic, while that for iDianiSnFR was endothermic.
source_text: The heats for iCytSnFR, iCyt_F_SnFR, and iCyt_BrEt_SnFR were exothermic, while that for iDianiSnFR was endothermic.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct observation from isothermal titration calorimetry experiments.

claim: All iDrugSnFRs show exergonic reactions, but the relative enthalpic and entropic contributions vary among iDrugSnFRs.
source_text: All iDrugSnFRs show exergonic reactions, but the relative enthalpic and entropic contributions vary among iDrugSnFRs.
evidence_reasoning: This is a thermodynamic analysis based on ITC data showing that all reactions are thermodynamically favorable but with different energetic contributions.

claim: iDrugSnFRs do not have pseudo-first-order kinetic behaviors typical of two-state binding interactions.
source_text: The stopped-flow data revealed that iDrugSnFRs do not have pseudo-first-order kinetic behaviors typical of two-state binding interactions.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from stopped-flow kinetic experiments showing complex binding kinetics.

claim: Most of the fluorescence change for iDianiSnFR occurs within the first 0.1 s of mixing.
source_text: Most of the fluorescence change occurs within the first 0.1 s of mixing (Figure 5A), with only minor additional increase by 100 s.
evidence_reasoning: This is a kinetic observation from stopped-flow experiments.

claim: Changes in fluorescence from iCytSnFR during the first 1 s of mixing fit well to a single exponential and have close to pseudo-first-order kinetics.
source_text: Changes in fluorescence from iCytSnFR during the first 1 s of mixing fit well to a single exponential (Figure 5B) and have close to pseudo-first-order kinetics (i.e., the observed rate of fluorescence change is nearly linear with drug concentration).
evidence_reasoning: This is a kinetic analysis from stopped-flow experiments showing the mathematical behavior of the binding kinetics.

claim: The aberrations from ideal first-order kinetics vitiate generation of definitive koff and kon values.
source_text: The aberrations from ideal first-order kinetics vitiate generation of definitive koff and kon values but we can approximate a Kmax and KD from our fitting procedures.
evidence_reasoning: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations in kinetic analysis due to the complex binding behavior observed.

claim: The kinetics of iDrugSnFR binding involve complexities beyond a simple first-order kinetic model governing two binding partners.
source_text: Our stopped-flow experiments reinforced previous observations (Unger et al., 2020) that the kinetics of iDrugSnFR binding involve complexities beyond a simple first-order kinetic model governing two binding partners.
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from stopped-flow experiments that confirms prior observations by Unger et al., 2020.

claim: The rank order of the iCytSnFR steady-state sensitivities is varenicline > cytisine > ACh.
source_text: The rank order of the iCytSnFR steady-state sensitivities is varenicline > cytisine > ACh.
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative ranking based on dose-response measurements in the microperfusion system.

claim: The time constant for decay decreased with increasing steady-state EC50 of the ligands, as though more tightly binding ligands dissociate more slowly.
source_text: The time constant for decay decreased with increasing steady-state EC50 of the ligands, as though more tightly binding ligands dissociate more slowly (Figure 6A).
evidence_reasoning: This is an observed correlation from microperfusion experiments with an inferred mechanistic explanation.

claim: The decay of the ACh response followed a single exponential time course with a mean koff of 1.9 ± 0.1 s–1.
source_text: Decay of the ACh response followed a single exponential time course (Figure 6B). The values of the koff for 30, 100, and 200 µM ACh did not differ significantly (ANOVA, p=0.62, degrees of freedom [df] = 2 (model), 20 [error]). We pooled them to obtain a mean koff of 1.9 ± 0.1 s–1 (mean ± SEM, n = 23 areas [50 cells]).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative kinetic measurement from microperfusion experiments with statistical analysis.

claim: The temporal resolution of the CytSnFR_PM sensor for changes in ACh concentration was in the subsecond range.
source_text: Hence, the temporal resolution of the CytSnFR_PM sensor for changes in the ACh concentration was in the subsecond range.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about sensor performance based on the measured decay kinetics.

claim: The decay of the cytisine and varenicline response was biphasic.
source_text: The decay of the cytisine and varenicline response was biphasic (Figure 6C and D): two exponential decay terms with an additional constant component fitted the cytisine decay significantly better than a single exponential term (F-test, p<0.05).
evidence_reasoning: This is a kinetic observation from microperfusion experiments with statistical validation of the fitting model.

claim: The kfoff and ksoff for 5–15 µM cytisine were 0.61 ± 0.04 s–1 and 0.146 ± 0.006 s–1, respectively.
source_text: The kfoff and ksoff for 5–15 µM cytisine were 0.61 ± 0.04 s–1 (n = 36 areas, 105 cells) and 0.146 ± 0.006 s–1 (n = 35 areas, n = 103 cells), respectively.
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative kinetic measurements from microperfusion experiments.

claim: The temporal resolution of CytSnFR_PM sensor for cytisine was less than 10 s.
source_text: Therefore, the temporal resolution of CytSnFR_PM sensor for cytisine was <10 s, adequate for the temporal resolution of the live-cell experiments presented below.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about sensor performance based on the measured decay time constants.

claim: The decay waveform of the varenicline response was much slower than that for cytisine or ACh.
source_text: Interestingly, the decay waveform of the varenicline response was much slower than that for cytisine or ACh (Figure 6A and D).
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative observation from microperfusion experiments.

claim: The values of the kfoff and ksoff for varenicline were 0.9 ± 0.2 s–1 and 0.0065 ± 0.0002 s–1, respectively.
source_text: The values of the kfoff and ksoff were 0.9 ± 0.2 s–1 and 0.0065 ± 0.0002 s–1, respectively (n = 4 areas [nine cells]).
evidence_reasoning: These are quantitative kinetic measurements from microperfusion experiments with varenicline.

claim: The temporal resolution of the iCytSnFR_PM sensor for varenicline was in the minute range.
source_text: Thus, the temporal resolution of the iCytSnFR_PM sensor for varenicline was in the minute range.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference about sensor performance based on the slow decay kinetics measured for varenicline.

claim: It would not be possible to resolve the differences between varenicline at the PM and in the ER in live-cell experiments using iCytSnFR.
source_text: In the live-cell experiments described below, it would not be possible to resolve the differences between varenicline at the PM and in the ER.
evidence_reasoning: This is a prediction about experimental limitations based on the slow kinetics of varenicline-iCytSnFR interactions.

claim: The relatively high affinity of iCytisineSnFR for varenicline arises in part from the increased lifetime of the varenicline-iDrugSnFR complex.
source_text: The relatively high affinity of iCytisineSnFR for varenicline, which presumably arises in part from the increased lifetime of the varenicline-iDrugSnFR complex, has drawbacks.
evidence_reasoning: This is an inferred mechanistic explanation for the high affinity based on the measured slow dissociation kinetics.

claim: iDianiSnFR showed a robust response to dianicline at the PM and the ER in HeLa cells across a range of concentrations (3.125‒100 µM).
source_text: iDianiSnFR showed a robust response to dianicline at the PM and the ER in HeLa cells across a range of concentrations (3.125‒100 µM), and the speed was nearly limited by solution exchanges
evidence_reasoning: This is a finding from live-cell fluorescence imaging experiments.

claim: At 100 µM dianicline, the PM and ER have a ΔF/F0 of approximately 1.2, but at lower concentrations, the ER displayed 30–75% of the signal detected at the PM.
source_text: At 100 µM, the PM and ER have a ΔF/F0 of ~1.2, but at lower concentrations, the ER displayed 30–75% of the signal detected at the PM, which may indicate a difference in membrane crossing (Figure 7A).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative observation from live-cell imaging comparing PM and ER signals.

claim: Cytisine showed slower entry into and exit from the ER of HeLa cells compared to the PM.
source_text: Cytisine showed slower entry into and exit from the ER of HeLa cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a kinetic observation from time-resolved fluorescence imaging in live cells.

claim: The iCytSnFR_PM construct detected cytisine at concentrations from 0.078 to 80 µM and demonstrated a return to baseline fluorescence upon washout on the order of seconds.
source_text: The iCytSnFR_PM construct detected cytisine at concentrations from 0.078 to 80 µM and demonstrated a return to baseline fluorescence upon washout on the order of seconds after each drug application, reaching a maximum ΔF/F0 of ~2 at concentrations above 5 µM (Figure 7B).
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative finding from live-cell imaging experiments.

claim: The iCytSnFR_ER construct only detected cytisine with a ΔF/F0 above the buffer control in the range of concentrations from 1.25 to 80 µM with a ΔF/F0 which was 25–50% of the maximum ΔF/F0 detected at the PM.
source_text: In contrast to the _PM construct, the iCytSnFR_ER construct only detected cytisine with a ΔF/F0 above the buffer control in the range of concentrations from 1.25 to 80 µM with a ΔF/F0, which was 25–50% of the maximum ΔF/F0 detected at the PM.
